title: The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
examples: Which wonder was built in Egypt?
What was the Colossus of Rhodes like?
Do all the wonders still exist today?

explain.say: Today we explore the seven wonders of the ancient world. These were amazing structures built long ago. We will learn about some famous ones today.

draw.text: The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World

explain.say: The Great Pyramid of Giza was a huge tomb for pharaohs. It shows amazing early Egyptian building skills. Think about the massive stones used to build it.
Next we look at the Hanging Gardens of Babylon. People thought they were built on a hillside. They were famous for their beautiful flowers and plants.
The Colossus of Rhodes was a giant statue of a god. It stood at the harbor entrance. It was very large and impressive to see.
The Lighthouse of Alexandria was a very tall tower. It helped sailors find their way safely at night. It was a guiding light for ships.
These wonders show us how advanced ancient civilizations were. They used amazing engineering skills. They built things to last for many years.

faq.a: The Pyramids of Giza are the only ones that largely remain visible today. They are very well preserved structures.
asks: Are any of the wonders still around?
Can we still see the ancient wonders?

faq.a: They were built to show off the power and wealth of the people who built them. They were great feats of engineering.
asks: What was the purpose of these buildings?
Did they have a special job?

faq.q: Were all seven wonders built at the same time?
faq.a: No, they were built across many different centuries. Different cultures built them in different eras.
asks: Did they happen all at once?
Was there a timeline for them?

faq.q: What was the Colossus made of?
faq.a: It was a massive statue, often described as being made of bronze. It was a tribute to a great victory.
asks: What material was the statue made from?

faq.a: They were famous gardens built in layers on a structure. They were known for their beautiful, exotic plants.

facts: The Pyramids of Giza were built for pharaohs in ancient Egypt.
The Lighthouse of Alexandria was a very tall navigational aid.
The Hanging Gardens were famous for their beautiful, tiered planting.
The Colossus of Rhodes was a gigantic statue at a harbor.

quiz.say: Which wonder is most associated with pharaohs?
quiz.why: The pyramids were built primarily as tombs for Egyptian pharaohs.

wrong.1: The lighthouse was for sailors, not for tombs.
wrong.2: The Colossus was a statue, not a burial site.
wrong.3: The gardens were for beauty, not for royal burials.

quiz.say: If a city needed a guiding light for ships, which wonder would fit?
quiz.why: Lighthouses are specifically designed to guide ships at sea.

wrong.0: Pyramids were inland tombs, not sea guides.
wrong.1: The statue was decorative, not a navigational tool.
wrong.2: Gardens are for plants, not for guiding ships.

quiz.say: Which wonder was known for its layered, beautiful plants?
quiz.why: The description of layered plants matches the Hanging Gardens.

wrong.0: The lighthouse is a tower for light.
wrong.2: Pyramids are made of stone, not plants.
wrong.3: The Colossus was a giant statue figure.
